content.text:
I read it. The link is a 7,395-byte Markdown file titled "Brief: one busy state between the app and the chat page", and it is byte-for-byte the same as [busy-state-cleanup-brief.md](busy-state-cleanup-brief.md) in the repository root (the SHA-256 checksums match). I have not started any of the work it describes.

**What the brief says**

- **The problem.** The chat panel is a web page inside JusPrin. It greys out New chat, Resume, Delete and Retry while the app is busy. The app decides "busy" from six inputs in `AgentHost::transition_busy()`, but sends it to the page in two kinds of message with two different meanings, from about 30 places that are not tied to where busy changes.
- **The visible mismatch.** The full state message carries all six inputs. The chat-list message carries only two of them (a reply streaming, or a tool result waiting). So a chat-list refresh during a slice would tell the page "not busy" while the app is busy. The brief says this comes from reading the code and has not been reproduced.
- **The page side.** The page mixes three inputs to decide what to grey out: its own guess that a reply is streaming, the app's `conversationBusy`, and `projectChatBlocked`.
- **The proposed design.** The brief marks this as a proposal whose details you have not approved. It has four parts:
  - `transition_busy()` is the only place that decides busy.
  - One function sends busy to the page, after each unit of work, and only when the value changed.
  - The page reads only that flag.
  - The app keeps its own check on each click, as it does today.
- **First thing to find out.** Whether every path that changes one of the six inputs reaches the main thread through a place where that one sender can run, especially tool work that finishes on another thread.
- **How to work.** Branch from `jusprin-dev`, do not push, and reproduce the mismatch in the shell harness before changing anything. Write host and page tests that fail first. Then run the listed test suites and harness modes against a scratch data directory.

The line numbers in the brief are from branch `error-sites` at commit ba4842b209, which the brief says is not yet on `jusprin-dev`.

Opening the link directly in Chrome left the tab on the New Tab page, so Chrome may have saved a copy of the file to your Downloads folder. I did not check Downloads.

Forget about the proposed design. It may not work well. You are a much more knowledgeable agent. So now you go look at the code base to verify if the brief got the problem correctly. Then check online or use your own knowledge to determine if the current code is the best way to handle this. Based on my understanding, this is a common problem that most web-based applications will face, which is probably 90% of the code in the world. So there gotta be some existing pattern or solution that we can borrow from

- **The core rule:** Information you can work out from props or existing state during rendering shouldn't be stored in that component's state.

- **Memoization:** useMemo is worth reaching for only when profiling shows a real cost.
- **Lint rule:** The `set-state-in-render` lint page shows "derive during render" examples, such as sorting `items` directly in the render body (Derive during render).

The brief has the core problem right: the app works out "busy" in two different ways, and the chat page keeps its own copy fed from three sources. It gets three details wrong, and one of them makes the fix much simpler than the brief assumed. Nothing below was run in the app; it is all from reading the code on `jusprin-dev` and `error-sites`.

## What the brief gets right

- The app's full answer uses six inputs ([AgentHost.cpp:3576](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3576)) and goes out in the full state message ([AgentHost.cpp:912](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:912)).
- The chat-list message sends a narrower answer that uses only two of them ([AgentHost.cpp:951](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:951)).
- The page overwrites its copy from whichever message came last ([store.ts:234](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/state/store.ts:234) and [store.ts:271](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/state/store.ts:271)), then mixes in its own guess that a reply is streaming ([App.tsx:426](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:426)).
- Nothing sends the page a new value when busy changes.

## What the brief gets wrong

- **Its example is narrower than it says.** When the AI itself starts a slice, the chat-list message does say busy, because a tool result is waiting. The mismatch needs a tool that no reply is waiting on, such as one started by an outside program through MCP. The test harness starts its slice that way too.
- **It misses the opposite failure.** On `error-sites`, a refused click resends the full state, so the page greys the buttons. When the tool finishes, the app sends only a tool message, which the page ignores for busy. My reading is that the buttons then stay grey until some unrelated message arrives.
- **Other threads are not involved.** The chat host has no threads. A 33 ms timer ([ShellController.cpp:363](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:363)) polls the reply, the tools and AI setup, so every change happens on the main thread.

Also, AI setup never greys the buttons at all: starting it sends only a setup message.

## Is the current code the best way

No. It breaks two well-known rules.

- **Keep one copy and work the rest out.** React's docs say not to store what you can calculate, and Redux's style guide says to keep state minimal and derive the rest. Here a calculated value is stored on the page and calculated twice in the app.
- **Send the current value, not the changes.** Kubernetes' API conventions call this level-based rather than edge-based, and say it is what survives missed changes. Here the page is right only if the right message happens to go out at every change.

A third rule, that the server checks every command whatever the client drew, is already followed. That one is from my own knowledge, not a source I fetched.

## What I would borrow (my proposal, not prototyped)

Use the timer that already exists. On each tick, in one place inside the host, compare `transition_busy()` with the value last sent and send a small message if it differs. The page stores that value from that message only. The chat-list flag, the page's fill-in and the page's own streaming guess are removed from the greying decision.

The brief's design had to list every path that changes busy and prove none was missed. This one reads the value itself every tick, so no list is needed. The cost is up to 33 ms of delay, which the app's own check on each click already covers.

It fails if the timer is not running while a chat page is showing. The Preferences window and the printer panel drive their own hosts, so the check must sit in a function all three call.

## Decision needed

Should I reproduce the wrong button state in the real app and then prototype the timer check? It is yours because it needs an app build on the shared Mac and you asked only for analysis. Saying yes costs a build and a harness run, and gives you evidence before any design is agreed. Saying no leaves this as code reading. My pick is yes, reproduction first.

content.text:
I surveyed every button the fork owns, after your side session relayed "broaden the scope to all fork-owned buttons". The chat page's busy value turns out to be one of two separate problems, and the second one is more widespread. Everything below is from reading code; nothing was reproduced in the app or changed.

## Problem one: a value the app owns, copied onto a page

This is the brief's problem. Outside the chat page's busy value I found only two more cases:

- **Blocked project chat.** If restoring an earlier chat fails, the app marks the project chat blocked but never tells the page, so Restore stays enabled.
- **Connecting an outside AI tool in Preferences.** The page and the app each keep their own copy of the previewed change, and the two can differ.

The rest is sound:

- **Home** sends values such as "can rename this printer" from a timer that compares with the last value sent ([HomeHost.cpp:112](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeHost.cpp:112)).
- **Native menus** are asked by wxWidgets in idle time and answer fresh each time.
- **The Slice button** works its state out fresh on each refresh.

## Problem two: a page greys a button and waits for an answer that never comes

A person clicks, the page greys the button itself, and it waits for some later message. Three things make this fragile:

- The pages have no shared way to send a message and wait for its answer ([bridgeClient.ts:158](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/WebShared/bridgeClient.ts:158)).
- When the app fails unexpectedly, it reports the failure and sends the page nothing ([AgentWebView.cpp:310](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:310), [HomeWebView.cpp:164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeWebView.cpp:164)).
- Some handlers return early without sending anything.

| Screen | What the person does | What they would see |
|---|---|---|
| Import from OrcaSlicer window | Clicks Import, cancels the unsaved-changes question | "Importing…" with Cancel grey; no failure needed |
| Home, print report | Sends a report and recording it fails | "Sending…" with every control grey |
| Home, first-run import | Import fails | "Importing…" until some other message arrives |
| Home and chat, add a printer | Adding the printer fails | Continue or the filament rows stay grey |
| Preferences, account | Try again gets a malformed model list | Try again stays grey |
| Preferences, connect an AI tool | The settings file cannot be written | "Writing settings…" with no buttons |

A related case: Preferences never shows the app's refusal message, so a refused click looks like nothing happened.

## Patterns to borrow

- **For problem one:** send the current value by compare-and-send on the existing timer, as Home already does. This is what I proposed before, and the fork has its own precedent.
- **For problem two:** the JSON-RPC rule, which says the server must reply to every request. My proposal is that a message expecting an answer always gets exactly one, success or failure, tied to that message's id. The page's waiting state then becomes "this request has no answer yet". The app already stamps most answers with that id; the page ignores it.

Neither is prototyped. The second has an open question: answers that arrive later, after a network call or a dialog, need the same guarantee.

## What I did not check

- I spot-checked the three background traces' main findings, not every line.
- The native side got a lighter read than the web pages.
- `jusprin-dev` moved during this session. The refused-click change from the brief's branch landed as commit f52f37375d, so the line numbers in my first report are off by about 13.

## Decision needed

Should I reproduce these stuck buttons in the real app before any design is agreed? It is yours because it needs an app build on the shared Mac and several driven runs. Yes gives you evidence for each row above and shows which ones are real. No leaves all of it as code reading. My pick is yes, starting with the OrcaSlicer import window, because it needs no failure to trigger.

Sources:
- [JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification)
- [Kubernetes API conventions](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md)
- [wxUpdateUIEvent](https://docs.wxwidgets.org/3.2/classwx_update_u_i_event.html)
Yes, reproduce them

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

During Phase 4 (2026-08-30), a background build "ran" for 5 hours: the
machine slept, the build paused, the 10-minute task timeout never fired, and
no completion notification arrived. I sat waiting instead of noticing.

**Why:** Background-task notifications are not guaranteed (sleep, wedged
timeouts). A silent wait looks identical to progress.

**How to apply:** For any background job expected to take more than a couple
of minutes: (1) check `date` and the process's CPU-time (`ps`) when resuming
work — near-zero CPU over long wall-clock means stalled or slept, not
working; (2) prefer a bounded Monitor (until-loop + explicit timeout) over
waiting for completion notifications; (3) when the user returns after a gap,
re-verify liveness of anything left running before reporting status.

---

Met on 2026-11-18 while adding a shell-harness scenario (`--orca-messages`, prototype only, uncommitted).

- `PrintHostJobQueue` deletes `upload_data.source_path` after the upload ends, success or error. A test that enqueues a job must give it a copy or a generated file. Handing it `tests/data/test_stl/ASCII/20mmbox-LF.stl` deleted that tracked file; every later harness run then failed at startup with "The file does not contain any geometry data." Fix: `git restore <file>`. JusPrin's own "Print again" copies the kept file for this reason (GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp).
- `tests/shell/dialog_witness.hpp` closes one window per 300 ms tick and takes the oldest shown dialog first. If a box from a queued event (for example OrcaSlicer's Info box) is still open when a case opens a second modal box, the witness keeps ending the outer one, which cannot unwind, and the run hangs printing "HARNESS DIALOG CLOSED" forever. Make each step's `done` wait until no modal wxDialog is shown.
- A killed or stalled harness run can leave the next run stalling once; repeat before reading anything into it. The print-issues mode's "press on the pill" checks fail in roughly 1 run in 6 on the unchanged app.

content.text:
I think you are right to challenge it, and I would drop the bigger design I proposed. I would not use a timeout either: there is a smaller fix that does better than a timeout for about the same amount of code.

## Why the bigger design is not worth it

- **Almost every stuck case needs the app to fail first.** Six of the seven I found only happen after an unexpected failure, which is rare by definition.
- **Real users are not reporting it.** I searched JusPrin's error reports just now. There are three kinds of report in total, all since 2026-11-19, and none is a failure while handling a page's message. That is weak evidence, because reporting is two days old and opt-in, but it is the only data there is.
- **The one case that needs no failure is a one-line bug.** In the Import from OrcaSlicer window, cancelling the unsaved-changes question returns without telling the page. That needs one line, not a design.
- **The chat page already heals itself.** It asks the app for its full state every 30 seconds, so a wrong busy value there lasts half a minute at most.

## Why a timeout is the wrong small fix

No single duration works. On 2026-11-05 the same first-launch import took 46 seconds with the screen unlocked and 226 seconds locked. A timeout shorter than that re-enables Import while the import is still running. A timeout longer than that fires after the person has already closed the window. It also tells the person nothing about what happened.

## What I would do instead (proposal, not built)

- **Tell the page when its message failed.** The app already catches every failed page message in one place per page. That place would send the page one "that failed" message, and each waiting button would clear on it. The button comes back at the moment of the failure, with no duration to guess.
- **Fix the import window's early return** with its one line.

- Settled by his decisions: drop it from "open".
- Outside the request: a follow-up, reported separately.
- Still needing work or his answer: wait for that.

content.text:
Three of the four kinds of stuck button reproduced in the app. The fourth, the chat page's busy value that the original brief was about, I could only produce artificially, and I now think a real person cannot reach it. Nothing is fixed yet.

## What I ran and what the app showed

| Kind of failure | What the person does | What the app showed | Real? |
|---|---|---|---|
| A wait the app never answers, no failure | In the Import from OrcaSlicer window, presses Import, then Cancel on the unsaved-changes question | "Importing…" with Cancel greyed for the 46 seconds I watched | Yes |
| A wait left hanging by a failure | In Preferences, connects Cursor while the folder holding its settings file is read-only | The error report window opens; after closing it the page stays on "Writing settings…" for 45 seconds, until another section is opened | Yes |
| A refusal the person cannot see | In Preferences, presses Connect… on Claude Code, leaves the section, comes back, presses Connect… again while the first command still runs | The app refuses with "A connection is already being saved." The page shows nothing for 16 seconds, then jumps to "Connected" | Yes, but harmless |
| A value the app owns goes stale | Presses New chat while the app is busy with a tool no reply is waiting on | Could not be reached with real actions | No |

## Why the chat page case is not reachable

- **A running slice is not "busy".** The slice tool finishes the moment the slice starts; the slice itself is not counted. The brief's example, and my reports that repeated it, were wrong on this.
- **A tool from an outside program runs within one 33 ms timer tick.** Nobody can press New chat in that window.

To check the mechanism anyway, I held a tool running with the test's own pacing knob, which no real tool does. The page then behaved as I had read it: New chat stayed enabled while the app was busy, greyed after a press, came back after a chat rename, and was still greyed when the tool ended. It came back within 5 seconds; I did not find which message did that.

## How this was run

These ran in the project's test harness, which is the real app shell with its real pages. Clicks went through the pages' own buttons. The fixtures were a stand-in OrcaSlicer folder with three printers, a scratch home folder, and a stand-in `claude` command that sleeps 25 seconds. I did not test the import window's title-bar close.

Pictures and run logs are in [.claude/stuck-buttons-shots](.claude/stuck-buttons-shots). The temporary test steps are uncommitted in my own worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/stuck-buttons-repro`.

## What this means

- **The chat page needs nothing.** I withdraw both the timer proposal and the one-line change for it.
- **The import window is a plain bug.** I will fix it whichever way you decide below; it needs no failure and leaves the person with a dead window.
- **The refused second press does no harm**, so I would leave it.

## Decision needed

Which fix should I build for the buttons that wait on the app? It is yours because it sets how much new code goes in. The small fix is the import bug plus one "your message failed" notice from the place that already catches every failed page message, so waiting buttons come back at once; that is a few dozen lines and would have un-stuck the Cursor case. Fixing the import bug only is one line and leaves the Cursor-style cases stuck after a failure, though the person can leave the screen. The full every-message-gets-an-answer design covers the most and costs the most. My pick is the small fix.

content.text:
Partly. Sentry captures the stuck states that come after a failure, so I will leave those unfixed as you said. It cannot see the import window bug, because nothing fails there.

## What Sentry captures

- **Stuck after a failure: yes, with a condition.** In the Cursor run, the app reported one unexpected error when the settings file could not be written. That report names what the app was doing, for example "handling the app page's mcp_connect message", and the error. The other five failure cases from my survey go through the same reporting function, from reading the code.
- **The condition is the person's consent.** The report reaches Sentry only if the person has automatic reports turned on, or presses send in the report window ([ErrorReport.cpp:42](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.cpp:42)). If they close the window, nothing is sent.
- **What arrives is the failure, not the stuck screen.** Sentry will show that writing the file failed. It will not say the page was left on "Writing settings…". We would know that from this survey.

So far Sentry holds no report of this kind, from two days of reporting.

## What Sentry cannot see

- **The import window stuck on "Importing…".** The app returns early when the person cancels the unsaved-changes question. Nothing throws, so nothing is reported, and no number of users hitting it would ever show up.
- **A refused press the page does not show.** The app's refusal is an ordinary message to the page, not a failure, so it is not reported either. This one does no harm.

## What I am doing

- **Leaving the failure cases alone.** If reports of failed page messages start arriving, that is the signal to revisit them.
- **Leaving the chat page alone.** It was not reachable in real use.
- **Leaving the refused press alone.**

The import window bug is the one case your condition does not cover: it is reproduced, it needs no failure, and waiting for Sentry will never surface it. The fix is one line plus a test, on its own branch.
